clips.text: Your tongue has around ten thousand taste buds — and it can also see.
He is blind — and he is climbing a rock wall, reading every hold with his tongue.
Four hundred tiny pulses — and within fifteen minutes, he can tell where things are.
He plays tic-tac-toe with his daughter. He reads letters off cards. He climbs.
The camera films the world. His tongue feels the picture.
So why can your tongue work as a second pair of eyes?
Your brain builds the picture, not your eyes — and the price is you can't taste while you see.
